title: Automated DNA Purification Using Bravo Workstation
author: Ayinuer Aximu Petri
materials: Start the FluidX barcode reader software and allow the camera to initialize.

Prepare reagents (sodium acetate), buffers (Binding buffer D, TET, PE) and aliquots of extraction positive controls (EPCs) and (optionally) purification negative controls (PNCs) as described in MATERIALS.
Decontaminate reagents and consumables as described in MATERIALS.

Log into the VWworks software using the administrator account (password "a"). Load the DNA extraction preparation protocol under "S:\Bravo_protocols\MPI-EVAN-homebrew\forms\DNA_extraction\V2_Extraction_purification_96.VWForm". Initialize the system.
Resuspend the beads in 1,000 μl of the binding buffer/sodium acetate mixture from go to step #9 by vigorous vortexing. Briefly centrifuge the tube.

Log into the VWworks software using the administrator account (password "a"). Load the DNA extraction preparation protocol under "S:\Bravo_protocols\MPI-EVAN-homebrew\forms\DNA_extraction\V2_Extraction_purification_96.VWForm". Initialize the system.

steps.title: Create extraction summary table
steps.instruction: In MS Excel, generate a table named ExPl_XXX listing the 96‑well FluidX rack layout with sample DNA lysates and their corresponding extraction negative controls (ENCs); reserve four positions per quarter for extraction positive, library negative and library positive controls (EPCs, LNCs, LPCs) using empty tubes as placeholders; if no ENCs exist, use purification negative controls (PNCs); reposition controls between runs for unbiased monitoring; save the sheet on the core‑unit server at \SummaryTables\Extractions\year using the provided TEMPLATE_ExPl_XX_SummaryTable_JJJJMMDD.xlsx.

steps.title: Prepare FluidX sample rack
steps.instruction: Assemble a FluidX rack containing 96 screw‑cap tubes each holding 150 µl of sample DNA lysate; store the rack at room temperature for same‑day extractions, at 4 °C for extractions within 4 weeks, or at –20 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Add lysates and controls to rack
steps.instruction: Place the lysate tubes, EPCs, ENCs (or PNCs), and empty placeholder tubes for future LNCs and LPCs into the rack according to the extraction summary table; record batch information for EPCs in Labfolder.

steps.title: Barcode and label sample rack
steps.instruction: Use the FluidX barcode reader to scan the bottom barcodes of all tubes and the rack ID; verify that tube positions match the summary table; label the plate with "Lysates for ExPl_XXX", the date, and your initials.

steps.title: Create Labfolder entry for run
steps.instruction: In Labfolder, create a new entry named with the Labfolder template and the extraction plate ID; fill all required data‑element fields (including EPC batch info) to later generate the CoreDB entry.

steps.title: Thaw frozen sample rack
steps.instruction: If the rack was stored in the –20 °C freezer, place it on a ThermoShaker set to 37 °C and 200 rpm for at least 10 min; randomly pick tubes from the middle of the rack to confirm complete thawing before proceeding.

steps.title: Resuspend and transfer silica beads
steps.instruction: Vortex the stock suspension of silica magnetic beads until fully resuspended with no pellet; transfer exactly 1,050 µl of the suspension into a 1.5 ml Safe‑Lock tube; pellet the beads in a magnetic rack (several minutes) and discard the clear supernatant.

steps.title: Wash silica beads twice
steps.instruction: For each of two washes: add 1,000 µl TET buffer to the bead tube, vortex, place on the magnetic rack, then pipette off and discard the supernatant; note that silica beads pellet strongly and must be mixed thoroughly; do not centrifuge after mixing; record the TET buffer batch in Labfolder.

steps.title: Combine bead suspension with binding buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire bead suspension into the binding‑buffer/sodium‑acetate mixture prepared in step 10; if any beads remain, rinse the 1.5 ml tube with additional binding‑buffer/sodium‑acetate until all beads are transferred.

steps.title: Prepare binding buffer mixture
steps.instruction: In a 250 ml bottle containing 157.5 ml binding buffer, add 6.3 ml sodium acetate; mix by shaking the bottle; use a dedicated pipette for sodium acetate and binding buffer because the mixture is corrosive; record the buffer and sodium acetate batch numbers in Labfolder.

steps.title: Power on Bravo system
steps.instruction: Switch on all Bravo components, including the external cooling device set to 4 °C, and turn on the hood light and ventilation ("Betrieb").

steps.title: Load tip boxes into stackers
steps.instruction: Unpack the 16 Bravo tip boxes, remove their lids, and load them into stackers 1‑2 of the BenchCel as indicated by the form file; optionally load only one box per stacker now and add the remaining boxes after the run has started.

steps.title: Fill and load buffer reservoirs
steps.instruction: Prepare two buffer reservoirs: fill one with approximately 60 ml PE buffer and the other with approximately 30 ml TET buffer; load both reservoirs into the MiniHub as specified in the form file; record the buffer batch numbers in Labfolder.

steps.title: Prepare empty rack for final extracts
steps.instruction: Take an empty FluidX rack for the final DNA extracts, scan all tube barcodes and the rack ID with the barcode reader, and save these identifiers in the extraction summary table.

steps.title: Label wash and elution plates
steps.instruction: Label a 96‑well LoBind PCR wash plate and a 96‑well LoBind PCR elution plate with the extraction plate ID, the words "wash plate" or "elution plate", the date, and your initials; place both plates into the MiniHub as indicated by the form file.

steps.title: Verify tip box placement
steps.instruction: If any tip boxes are still missing, add them to the stackers now and double‑check that all required deck positions are correctly filled.

steps.title: Start Bravo run and monitor
steps.instruction: Select the proper settings in the form file: Protocol = 5M40_DNA_Extraction_96; Elution volume = 15 µl (two elution steps for a final 30 µl); Plate type for lysate = 0.8 ml FluidX tubes; Plate type for final extract = 0.8 ml FluidX tubes; Reservoir type for Binding buffer = HTS; Reservoir type for PE and TE = HTS. Click the "Run" button in VWorks and load any remaining reagents/consumables within 40 min. The run lasts ~3 h: the first 15 min aliquot the bead suspension, then the robot transfers lysate to the bead suspension; the robot pauses ~3 min for visual inspection of pipetting success. Monitor that the robot pipettes correctly and that no tubes remain stuck on the head; if tubes are stuck, gently shake the rack from the right side of the Bravo deck—never touch the rack from the front side.

steps.title: Seal elution plate post‑run
steps.instruction: While the elution plate remains on the magnet, seal it with adhesive foil; inspect the plate for any bead carry‑over. If beads are present, store the plate in the freezer for 6 months for possible troubleshooting; if no beads are observed, discard the plate.

steps.title: Seal wash plate for storage
steps.instruction: Seal the wash plate with adhesive foil and store it in the freezer for 6 months.

steps.title: Clean robot and shut down
steps.instruction: Wipe the Bravo deck and surrounding benches with tissues and ethanol; switch off the robot and the external cooling device; restart the computer to enable remote access; finally, turn off the computer screen.

steps.title: Discard plastic ware and document
steps.instruction: Remove and discard all plastic ware remaining in the robot (except the liquid‑waste plates); check the lysate rack, plates, and reservoirs for any residual liquid to confirm that all pipetting steps were completed; if unexpected volumes remain, add comments in the Labfolder notes field and in the Mattermost experiment documentation.

steps.title: Dispose liquid waste and tips
steps.instruction: Pour liquid waste from the square‑well plates into 500 ml labelled bottles placed next to the sink using a funnel; discard used tips in regular trash and tip boxes in the large waste bin on the left side of the cooling unit.

steps.title: Close final extract tubes and store
steps.instruction: Using the lids stored on the 96‑well lid holder, carefully close the FluidX tubes that contain the final eluate; place the rack in the freezer until library preparation.

steps.title: Create Labfolder entry for plate assembly
steps.instruction: Before assembling any plate (e.g., wash or elution plate), create a Labfolder entry named with the Labfolder template and the extraction plate ID; fill all required data‑element fields to document the plate assembly.
